Our story

From a hackathon idea to connected compliance.

Medlock began as an AI code review tool at HackPrinceton. The questions we found there led us toward compliance—and into a continuing journey of building, researching, and testing new ways to make responsible AI work in practice.

01

How it started

One problem led us to a more important one.

What started at Princeton University as a tool for reviewing AI-generated code evolved into a broader mission: helping organizations understand, manage, and maintain compliance as AI becomes part of critical environments.

The journey so far

Built through iteration, research, and real-world constraints.

01
HackPrincetonPrinceton University

We started with AI code review.

Medlock’s first form was an AI code review tool built at HackPrinceton. That experience became the starting point for a deeper look at how organizations govern and trust AI systems.

02
The pivotCompliance management

We shifted toward compliance.

We built a compliance management tool and presented it at Tech Innovation Day at William Paterson University, where the project won the event.

Watch the compliance demo ↗
03
ResearchAlgorithms & architecture

Product work became research.

We began developing algorithms around the compliance problem and filed a provisional patent for our “Cryptographic Enclave AI Pipeline” on June 9, 2026.

04
HealthCom 2026Research acceptance

Our research reached the academic community.

Our research paper was accepted at HealthCom 2026, advancing the work from an early product direction into an accepted research contribution.

05
Open sourceGovernance tools

We contributed to the wider ecosystem.

Our team contributed to AgenTrust, which was acquired by Anthropic, and to Microsoft’s Agent Governance Toolkit (AGT).

06
Dell × NVIDIAHealthcare AI

We built for local, compliant AI.

At the Dell × NVIDIA Hackathon, we built an AI agent that runs locally in healthcare environments without sending work to third-party LLMs such as OpenAI or Claude. The project was featured by NVIDIA Healthcare on social media.

What shaped Medlock

What we learned

Compliance has to work where the data lives.

From cryptographic enclaves to local healthcare agents, our work keeps returning to the same idea: responsible AI depends on architectures that protect sensitive environments without disconnecting people from the context they need.
